source.title: Spectral Bias Outside the Training Set for Deep Networks in the Kernel Regime

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives bounds and reports NTK spectrum measurements that bear on the generalization claim, but its main result is a theoretical comparison of finite-width training dynamics to idealized kernel dynamics, not a direct test of the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports NTK spectra for LeNet-5 on MNIST and a shallow fully connected Softplus network on CIFAR-10. The remaining results are theoretical bounds and implications; cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional bounds on early spectral bias outside the training set and measures NTK spectra at initialization. Neither result tests V1–V8. Its width scaling is not a comparison of test error beyond interpolation, and its Hessian/Fisher analysis does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under the stated assumptions, finite-width networks trained on finite samples approximate population kernel dynamics up to a stopping time and inherit early spectral bias outside the training set. The bounds cover smooth fully connected, convolutional, and residual architectures and permit width and sample size to grow at the same rate. They do not characterize later target-dependent kernel adaptation.
record.recipe_differences: The main claim is established with theoretical bounds for gradient flow on squared loss, plus initialization-only NTK spectrum plots; it does not directly evaluate held-out error under the listed training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical bounds are limited to a stopping time and depend on architecture, initialization and input distribution; the paper says later target-dependent kernel adaptation is outside its framework. Figure 1 reports separate MNIST and CIFAR-10 spectra.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3.5 and Corollary 3.7 bound population L2 deviations from idealized kernel dynamics up to a stopping time. Observations 3.8–3.9 imply preferential early learning of top NTK eigenfunctions, including when width and sample size grow at the same rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated kernel-regime assumptions, finite networks inherit early spectral bias over the input distribution, with higher-eigenvalue NTK components learned faster.

fits_no_version.finding: Both initialization spectra have a few large outlier eigenvalues followed by many small eigenvalues.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The initialization NTK Gram matrices of the tested LeNet-5/MNIST and shallow Softplus/CIFAR-10 networks have strongly skewed spectra.

record.problems: The central conclusion is theoretical and conditional on assumptions, including antisymmetric initialization, smooth activations, and a stopping time. The plotted experiments measure initialization spectra only and do not measure generalization error. The authors state that later kernel adaptation is outside the framework.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the theorem and corollaries: they bound function-space deviation from kernel dynamics rather than report an experimental result as a number or explicit measured outcome. Cited studies' results are excluded.

untested.parts: No own comparison of random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and random-label held-out accuracy.
No test-error comparison across widths beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No held-out-error comparison between convolutional and fully connected networks or test of learned local connectivity.
No optimizer comparison or tuning-budget experiment.
No training-batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes. The 2000-example batches are used to compute initialization spectra.
No dropout or weight-decay intervention and held-out-error comparison.
No magnitude-scaled perturbation measurement, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Change the reader's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. Corollary 3.10 includes a conditional population squared-error bound, but it does not establish any listed comparison. The theoretical results are already declared in rows_left_out, and no additional results bearing on V1–V8 are missing.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels or compare natural-label train and held-out error.
Does not sweep width past the interpolation threshold or report test error versus width.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected classifiers' held-out error.
Does not compare adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers' held-out performance.
Does not vary batch size or measure a large-batch generalization gap.
Does not test dropout or weight decay effects on held-out error.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare generalization gaps across trained networks.
Does not remove memorized examples or measure resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: LeNet-5
rows.operation_detail: Computed the NTK Gram-matrix spectrum at initialization for the logit of class 0.

conditions.value: 10 random parameter initializations and data batches

rows.measure: Normalized NTK Gram-matrix eigenvalue magnitude versus eigenvalue index; authors describe a small number of large outliers followed by a long tail of small eigenvalues.
rows.note: Figure reports the spectrum, not train/test error or a measured generalization gap. The text describes the qualitative shape; no numerical values are stated.
rows.check: The extraction matches Figure 1 and Appendix F. Initialization eigenvalues do not establish any listed version; the qualitative spectral pattern is stated, but no numerical eigenvalues are supplied in the text.

rows.operation_detail: Computed the NTK Gram-matrix spectrum at initialization.

conditions.value: 10 random parameter initializations and data batches

rows.measure: Normalized NTK Gram-matrix eigenvalue magnitude versus eigenvalue index; authors describe a small number of large outliers followed by a long tail of small eigenvalues.
